sources.title: Public biographical preview: 24 April 1971 birth and ministerial career
sources.findings: Read Munzinger’s publicly accessible biographical preview. It gives 24 April 1971 and the broad 2007 parliamentary, 2008–2011 education and 2012–2019 finance chronology. Its birthplace is Minj, whereas an indexed 2026 National feature describes a Tari birth journey; the latter body returned 403 and the conflict is not resolved by assumption. The public dossier retains the supported birthday and omits a precise birthplace. Huli identity is supported separately by SBS; Munzinger’s spelling Hulki and generalisations about community lifestyle are not copied. No subscription-only biography or birth record was accessed.

sources.title: James Marape profile: parliamentary and ministerial chronology, 2022 election and education
sources.findings: Read the ADB Development Asia speaker profile. It gives parliamentary service since 2007, education minister 2008–2011, finance minister 2012–2019, and the 9 August 2022 parliamentary prime-minister election. It separately records relinquishing Foreign Affairs and taking Treasury in January 2024: Finance and Treasury are distinct portfolios, not an office newly created in 2024. The education paragraph gives BA 1993, postgraduate honours in environmental/science studies in 2000 and MBA at UPNG. The dossier uses the BA year corroborated by SBS and does not invent the MBA year, degree certificate review or present Treasury/Foreign Affairs office.

sources.title: 31 May 2019 profile: Huli background, education, party changes and prior ministerial service
sources.findings: Read SBS’s 31 May 2019 profile, including the previous-day election, Huli background, university paragraph, first parliamentary entry under National Alliance, later PNC membership, finance portfolio and April 2019 departure leading to PANGU membership. It describes Tari-Pori in newly created Hela province in 2012. Its education sentence compresses BA and honours around 1993, while ADB separates honours into 2000; the public text omits the disputed honours date. Its passages on old loan/arrest controversies are not carried forward as current verdicts, and no criminal outcome is inferred from them.

sources.title: 30 May 2019 parliamentary election of Marape as prime minister after O’Neill’s resignation
sources.findings: Read ABC’s contemporaneous 30 May 2019 report through the election result, resource-policy pledges, earlier defections and succession passages. It explicitly records 101 votes to eight and O’Neill’s resignation the preceding day. This was parliamentary selection of a prime minister, not a nationwide direct presidential-style vote. The 31 May update is not the election date. Pledges to review resource laws and agreements are not completed revenue gains. The older ombudsman-loan allegations and responses are not used to assert a final legal finding or guilt.

sources.title: 9 August 2022: unopposed parliamentary election, coalition formation and incomplete national vote counting
sources.findings: Read ABC’s 9 August 2022 election report, updated the following day. It records an unopposed parliamentary election with unanimity among MPs present, while only 105 of 118 seat results had been presented and other counts were incomplete. PANGU had the most seats and assembled a multi-party coalition; this was not a single-party absolute majority or proof of nationwide unanimous voter support. Violence, interrupted counting and procedural controversies are reported as electoral context. No later court disposition of each disputed constituency or current 2026 no-confidence rules is inferred.

sources.publisher: US Government Publishing Office / Department of State
sources.title: Defense Cooperation Agreement, TIAS 23-816: signed 22 May 2023, entered into force 16 August 2023
sources.findings: Read the GovInfo catalogue record for State Department treaty publication TIAS 23-816. Its title and metadata explicitly identify Port Moresby signature on 22 May 2023 and entry into force on 16 August 2023. The automatic citation’s January 1 issue date is a bibliographic default, not a signature date. The PDF timed out, while legacy State Department pages returned technical-difficulty shells. No full treaty-text review, personal signature by Marape, precise facility-access provision or immunity analysis is claimed. The dossier describes his government’s agreement, not a document he necessarily personally signed.

sources.publisher: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.title: Papua New Guinea relationship page: Pukpuk Treaty signed 6 October 2025 and effective 8 July 2026
sources.findings: Read DFAT’s Papua New Guinea page sections on the Pukpuk Treaty and bilateral security cooperation. It explicitly gives Albanese and Marape as signatories on 6 October 2025 and entry into force on 8 July 2026, with alliance terminology. This mutual-defence treaty is distinguished from the older bilateral security agreement and the separate US defence agreement. The entire treaty and every implementation instrument were not reviewed; no transfer of national sovereignty or completed operational integration is asserted.

sources.title: F2026N00505: notice confirming Pukpuk Treaty entry into force on 8 July 2026
sources.findings: Read the complete short F2026N00505 entry-into-force notice. It states that the treaty done on 6 October 2025 entered into force for Australia on 8 July 2026. The Attorney-General dated the notice 13 July, and it was registered 14 July; neither date replaces the treaty’s commencement. The joint leaders’ 8 July Brisbane meeting statement separately confirms bilateral commencement. This is more precise evidence than an earlier announcement or a forecast about ratification.

sources.title: 17 November 2026 official report of Xi Jinping’s Shenzhen meeting with James Marape
sources.findings: Read the Chinese mission’s 17 November 2026 report of the completed Shenzhen meeting. It identifies Marape as PNG prime minister and describes trade, investment, infrastructure and multilateral cooperation proposals. These are government accounts of positions and plans, not audited economic achievements. Its claim of consistently following one-China policy over 50 years is attributed political rhetoric and is not imported as a comprehensive diplomatic history; the Reuters report notes a brief 1999 Taiwan relationship. No photographs or event video were inspected.

sources.title: 17 November 2026 meeting report: Marape’s comments on closing Taiwan’s office and Taiwan’s account
sources.findings: Read Reuters’s 17 November 2026 meeting report. It records Marape’s account of domestic difficulties surrounding closure of Taiwan’s office and Taiwan’s account blaming Beijing’s pressure. Keep these competing explanations attributed; do not present a contested sovereignty claim as settled or infer completion of future trade and energy measures.

sources.title: January 2024 democracy tracker: riots, pay protests and the 11 January emergency declaration
sources.findings: Read International IDEA’s January 2024 country-event summary and source list. It dates the two-week emergency to 11 January, following pay protests and riots, and explicitly attributes the administrative-error explanation to the government. It notes unemployment, inflation and low-wage discontent. Avoid collapsing the pay dispute into a proven new tax, treating suspension pending investigation as a conviction, or reporting its prospective no-confidence scenario as a vote that definitely happened. No fresh November 2026 labour, inflation or casualty series was audited; the summary gives historical governance context.

sources.publisher: PNG Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council
sources.title: 27 February 2024 report of Marape’s 23 February first-gold event and PNG stakeholder ownership
sources.findings: Read the PNG prime minister’s department’s 27 February 2024 report. It explicitly places the attended first-gold event on Friday 23 February and describes 51 percent combined PNG stakeholder equity, including State, Enga provincial and landowner interests. The combined share is neither Marape’s personal property nor wholly central-government ownership. The developer’s remaining 49 percent and Barrick’s own underlying interest must not be conflated. The event, publication date, ownership structure and future local benefits are distinct. Promises about improved living standards and community support are not independently evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: 22 December 2023: Porgera recommissioning begins, with production restart planned for early 2024
sources.findings: Read Barrick’s dated 22 December 2023 recommissioning release. It says the commencement agreement was completed that day, work to recommission began, and mining/processing restart was expected in the first quarter of 2024 after care and maintenance since April 2020. Thus the December agreement/preparation milestone is not already the February first gold pour or proof of full production. Indexed Q1 2024 corporate results separately confirm first gold on 23 February. The company’s resource potential and performance forecasts are not independently verified reserves or guaranteed economic results.

portraitReview.credit: Chuck Kennedy / U.S. Department of State; cropped by Ooligan
portraitReview.unresolved: Read crop and parent Commons descriptions, history, US federal-work notice and parent Flickr-review record dated 25 May 2023. Independently opened the Department of State Flickr source: it names Marape at the 22 May 2023 Port Moresby press availability, credits Chuck Kennedy and explicitly labels Public Domain/United States government work. Ooligan uploaded and cropped on 25 May, not the photographer. Parent is 4000×2668 (1.05 MB); crop 1168×1557 (542 KB), recorded as a lossless 71-percent horizontal/42-percent vertical crop. EXIF digitizing date 11 May differs from the 22 May capture/source caption, so it is not used to redate the event. The old 380697-byte cache record is absent and not evidence of original-image possession. Original download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000. Identity, original colour, framing and actual sharpness remain unreviewed; preserve source/creator credit and crop notice.
